post.title: Hello Sim and XO Space
post.hook: A one-screen iOS app built so Claude can tap, pinch and swipe its way through it.
post.summary: Two SwiftUI apps in one Xcode project: Hello Sim, a card-per-capability demo for driving the iOS Simulator with Claude, and XO Space, a native sample of the Space dashboard with a plan to ship it to the App Store.
post.writeup:
## What it is
One Xcode project holding two SwiftUI apps. **Hello Sim** is a single screen of cards. Each card exercises one thing Claude can do in the iOS Simulator, and a tag in its corner names the action that drives it. **XO Space** is a native iPhone and iPad sample of the XO Space dashboard.

## Why
Hello Sim is a test bench: it gives Claude a known app to attach to, build, launch, screenshot and drive. XO Space asks a different question: could the Space dashboard live on a phone as a companion app?

## How it works
Hello Sim maps actions like `tap`, `swipe`, `touch_path`, `touch2_path`, `open_url` and `button` to cards (Tap, Swipe, Drag, Pinch, Deep link, Home button). A swipe that starts within 4 points of a screen edge acts as the system gesture. For everything else Claude falls back to `xcrun simctl` (dark mode, fake GPS, push payloads, screen recording) and `xcodebuild`.

XO Space has four tabs: Projects, Agents, Inbox and Setup. It uses the dark "Grove" theme taken from the web UI's CSS, Swift Charts for token usage, and fictional data that mirrors the web preview server. It has its own bundle ID, `builders.xo.space`, an app icon and a privacy manifest.

## Findings
- The `inspect` action is documented but rejected by this build, so tap positions come from screenshots.
- Simulators only: no physical devices, no camera, no Face ID.
- APP_STORE_PLAN.md concludes XO Space cannot be submitted as is. It has no sign-in and only placeholder data, and apps built around placeholder content get rejected.

## Open questions
- The plan recommends a hosted-spaces companion backed by a read API in XO Swarm, with Clerk sign-in plus Sign in with Apple.
- It needs an organization developer account, a D-U-N-S number, and a Mac updated for a newer Xcode.
- It also suggests moving `XOSpace/` into its own repo before real work starts.
